title: Boot re-derives backlog from issue stage; handoff nextActions must not carry a backlog snapshot (kill stale-backlog telephone game)
description: The orchestrator handoff nextActions array is 100% LLM free-form prose; nothing deterministic populates or refreshes it. writeOrchHandoff (src/orchestrator/handoff.ts:53-59) is plumbing with no production caller; the agent hand-types the payload per the persona (src/vendor/_generated.ts:28). The respawn machinery is content-blind: run.ts:236-261 does a verbatim mv to .cam-orch-handoff.consumed.json, points CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE at it, and the fresh session ingests nextActions unchanged; cam journal append --cycle-close only arms the recycle marker and never touches handoff content. Critically, buildOrchestratorBootPrompt (src/commands/run.ts:155-181) reads CLAUDE.md, project.toml, journal.md, prd.json, git state, and the consumed handoff, but never reads scripts/cam/issues/*.json. A deterministic stage-based backlog deriver already exists (selectPlannableFromFile / selectPlannableIssue at src/issues/select.ts:29-82, filtering stage=specified AND status=open AND not blocked) but is wired only into the sidecar/plan path, not the orchestrator boot path. Consequence: a backlog item the LLM once typed into nextActions is copied forward verbatim across every respawn and never reconciled against the issue stage, so an already-shipped issue keeps reappearing as unblocked backlog. Observed 2-3 times; concretely, CAM-139 shipped 2026-07-05 09:11 (PR #135) yet the CAM-149 handoff written 2026-07-05 21:49 still listed CAM-139 as unblocked backlog, and the fresh boot greeted with it. Fix, two moves: (1) Boot injects a deterministic backlog block: extend buildOrchestratorBootPrompt to read scripts/cam/issues/*.json and inject a computed open-backlog listing grouped by stage (idea, specified, etc.) with blockedBy, reusing and generalizing the src/issues/select.ts stage logic so it lists all open issues, not just plannable ones; the greeting derives from this block, not from handoff nextActions. (2) nextActions becomes ephemeral-only: update the orchestrator persona (source under .claude/agents plus templates, which regenerate src/vendor/_generated.ts) and the handoff schema doc so nextActions carries only cycle-specific next-steps and never a backlog snapshot; the backlog is always derived, never hand-copied. This kills the whole class of stale-backlog propagation, not just the CAM-139 instance. Reuses existing select.ts; scope small-to-medium. Related but distinct: CAM-141 (handoff consume-before-read race, a delivery bug resolved via CAM-162) and CAM-172 (context backstop); this issue is content-staleness, not delivery.

spec.scope: CAM-190 subsumes CAM-74: build one deterministic cam issue list command as the single source of the actionable backlog, and wire the orchestrator to derive backlog from it (boot and on-demand), never from a handoff snapshot. IN SCOPE: (1) cam issue list deterministic branch: add a list subcommand to parseIssueArgs (index.ts discriminated union) without breaking cam issue "<text>" = create; route to a new runIssueList in src/commands/issue.ts that reads issues from main via readBacklogFromMain (NOT the thin-proxy send-keys path, NOT a claude spawn) and renders via the src/logging linear print helpers. (2) Render: group open issues by stage in lifecycle order (idea, specified, planned); exclude shipped and abandoned by default; --all includes shipped; columns priority, id, a [blocked: X] marker when blockedBy is unmet, truncated title; sort within a stage by priority ascending (1 first), tie-break id ascending (mirrors CAM-25). (3) Backend behavior: issue_system=none renders the table; linear and github print a short hint pointing at the native UI (gh issue list or the Linear app), never hard-fail. (4) Orchestrator wiring: buildOrchestratorBootPrompt (src/commands/run.ts) and the persona (.claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md plus templates) instruct deriving the backlog from cam issue list, with a fallback to reading scripts/cam/issues/*.json filtered by stage when the command is unavailable (old binary pre-rebuild). The one-screen greeting gains a single backlog line = live counts per stage; NO per-issue enumeration in the greeting. On-demand: whenever the operator asks what is in the backlog, run cam issue list fresh, never from memory or the handoff. (5) nextActions redefined as ephemeral cycle-continuation only; a hard rule states that NO handoff field enumerates the backlog; update orch-handoff.schema.json description accordingly. (6) Re-embed the persona and template edits into src/vendor/_generated.ts (bun run embed-vendor); diff .claude vs templates first per CAM-123 (copies may diverge per file). OUT OF SCOPE: --json output, --state filter, a full issue list for linear/github (hint only), 1.0.0 graduation, changing the stage enum, changing openState or keyDecisions or openQuestions semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: cam issue list over a fixture containing a stage:shipped status:open issue does NOT list that issue in the actionable backlog (the CAM-139 regression case).

cam issue list groups open issues by stage (idea, specified, planned) and excludes shipped and abandoned by default; --all includes shipped. Verified on a mixed-stage fixture asserting groups and counts.
Within each stage group, issues are sorted by priority ascending (1 first), tie-break id ascending.
An open issue with an unmet blockedBy renders a [blocked: X] marker.
cam issue list is deterministic: it reads issues from main and prints without spawning claude or tmux; a fake spawn asserts no pane or send-keys operations are invoked.
parseIssueArgs parses cam issue list as the list subcommand and still parses cam issue "<free text>" as create (no regression); both covered by unit tests.

Doc-gate test (CAM-61 style): the persona and boot prompt contain the instruction to derive the backlog via cam issue list, plus the rule that no handoff field enumerates the backlog; the greeting spec contains no per-issue enumeration.
issue_system=none renders the table; issue_system=linear or github prints a hint line pointing to the native UI and does not hard-fail. Verified per backend.

Boot backlog derivation prefers cam issue list; when the command is unavailable or exits non-zero, it falls back to reading scripts/cam/issues/*.json filtered by stage (works across the rebuild boundary).
gotchas: cam convention: a shipped issue keeps status:open with stage:shipped (140 such issues today), so the actionable backlog MUST filter by stage, never by status; filtering by status:open reintroduces the exact bug.
readBacklogFromMain reads issues from main via git cat-file --batch (source of truth), not the working tree; the list command must use it, not a raw fs read of the working dir.

cam issue list must branch to the deterministic read-and-render BEFORE the existing runIssue thin-proxy logic (which injects /cam-issue create into the orchestrator pane); it must not send-keys or spawn claude.
The .claude/agents and templates copies may diverge per file (CAM-123); diff before editing and re-embed into src/vendor/_generated.ts via bun run embed-vendor or the vendor-drift check fails.

binary and branch coherence: the installed cam binary will not have cam issue list until CAM-190 ships and the operator rebuilds; the boot fallback to reading issue files by stage keeps the orchestrator correct across that boundary.
stage enum is idea then specified then planned then shipped (planned, not planning).
domainTerms: actionable backlog: open issues whose stage is not shipped or abandoned (idea, specified, planned); the set the orchestrator and operator act on.
stage vs status: stage is the lifecycle position (idea, specified, planned, shipped); status is open or abandoned; a shipped issue stays status:open, so stage is the source of truth for the backlog.

backlog snapshot (anti-pattern): a hand-authored enumeration of open issues copied into the handoff nextActions; it propagates stale across respawns and is replaced by live derivation via cam issue list.
